function.mechanism: Hydrocolloid behavior: increases viscosity and stabilizes matrices; alginate systems form gel networks via ionic interactions, including calcium-mediated gelation behavior.

adi.basis: EFSA (2017) concluded no need for a numerical ADI (ADI not specified) for alginic acid and its salts (E400-E404).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses/levels; insufficient data for adequate assessment in certain infant and young-child FSMP categories.

adi.basis: JECFA listing for calcium alginate (INS 404): ADI NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: EFSA identified a data gap for infants and young children consuming foods for special medical purposes (FC 13.1.5.1 and 13.1.5.2), so safety could not be adequately assessed for those categories.

Recent rat data show sodium alginate can modulate gut microbiota and bile-acid/SCFA profiles with sex- and viscosity-dependent effects; adverse clinical significance for humans at food-additive exposures remains unclear.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation of E400-E404 found no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposure estimates for reported uses.
JECFA calcium alginate record reports ADI NOT SPECIFIED.
No IARC monograph classification entry identified for calcium alginate/alginic acid in the current IARC classifications dataset.

populations: infants and young children consuming FSMP (assessment data gap noted by EFSA)
adi_exceedance.notes: Numerical exceedance cannot be computed because EFSA/JECFA did not set a numeric ADI for E404; EFSA still flagged uncertainty for specific FSMP infant/young-child categories.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus (EFSA, FDA/CFR, JECFA) indicates low concern under authorized food-use conditions, but not enough evidence supports a fully risk-free classification due to unresolved pediatric medical-food data gaps and limited modern human long-term outcome data specific to E404.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed and no safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses
US CFR: GRAS status with explicit food-use conditions
No IARC classification entry found for calcium alginate
Uncertainty remains for infants/young children in FSMP categories
